title: Rabbah son of Rav Huna Zuta of Nehardea
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was the judge there, as in [Ketubot 69a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.69a.14), where Rav Nechemyah son of Rav Yosef sent to him: “When that woman comes before you, collect a tenth of the property for her.” Hyman identifies Rav Nechemyah as Rava’s student and infers that Rabbah son of Rav Huna Zuta was head in Nehardea in Rav Papa’s time.

Likewise in [Beitzah 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.29b.4): “Rava [Hyman proposes Rabbah, as in the Soncino printing and the She’iltot, Emor] son of Rav Huna Zuti expounded at the gate of Nehardea. Rav Nachman said: Go out and tell Abba (my colleague — [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Beitzah.29b.4.1-2)): We owe you no thanks for this,” etc. (Hyman considers “Rav Nachman” a scribal error and proposes, according to Dikdukei Soferim, Rav Chama; he endorses this reading, for Rav Chama too was head in Nehardea after Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, as cited in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 2.)[^1][^2]

notes.text: Ketubot names Rabbah and Beitzah names Rava. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3140&lang=en) discusses both notices. Rashi glosses “Abba” as “my colleague” and explains the reply as withholding thanks.
The Soncino and She’iltot wording, the Rav Chama replacement, and the chronology are Hyman’s reports and argument.
